title: Non-triazine photosystem II inhibitors provide effective control of metabolic atrazine-resistant Amaranthus tuberculatus.
authors: Lopez, Alexander J; Henry, Ryan S; Jacobs, Kip E; Raiyemo, Damilola A; Werle, Isabel S; Tranel, Patrick J
one_liner_zh: 该文研究除草剂对耐阿特拉津杂草的防效及PSII靶标分子对接，虽涉及蛋白-小分子对接，但对象为除草剂-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Overexpression of the Phi-class glutathione S-transferase (GST) AtuGSTF2 has been implicated in the detoxification of atrazine in Amaranthus tuberculatus (Moq.) Sauer (waterhemp). However, little is known about this GST and the susceptibility of resistant populations to other Photosystem II (PSII)-inhibitors remains unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the efficacy of non-triazine PSII-inhibitors amicarbazone and metribuzin against atrazine-resistant A. tuberculatus. Molecular docking analysis with these molecules was also conducted at the PSII target-site to further investigate differences in their relative potencies and recommended field-use rates. Furthermore, the AtuGSTF2 gene and translated protein structure were analyzed to identify potential regulatory relationships and characterize the active site. RESULTS: Compared to atrazine, amicarbazone improved the control of metabolic atrazine resistant populations to a greater extent than metribuzin, and control was further improved when amicarbazone and metribuzin were applied in a 1.75:1 mixture. Molecular docking indicated that amicarbazone interacts with the target site similarly to atrazine and metribuzin but with greater predicted affinity. Genomic and structural analyses suggest that AtuGSTF2 may be regulated by multiple transcription factors and the encoded protein exhibits substrate recognition promiscuity consistent with other GSTs. CONCLUSION: Together, these findings indicate that amicarbazone is a potent molecule and offers a more effective alternative to atrazine than metribuzin for managing at least some NTS atrazine-resistant A. tuberculatus populations. However, tank-mixing amicarbazone with metribuzin can provide even more effective control than either herbicide alone. Furthermore, substrate recognition promiscuity could possibly endow AtuGSTF2 with the potential for broader metabolic cross-resistance. (c) 2026 The Author(s). abstract_zh: 背景：Phi类谷胱甘肽S-转移酶（GST）AtuGSTF2的过表达已被认为与Amaranthus tuberculatus (Moq.) Sauer（水麻）中阿特拉津的解毒有关。然而，关于该GST的了解甚少，且抗性种群对其他光系统II（PSII）抑制剂的敏感性仍不清楚。因此，本研究评估了非三嗪类PSII抑制剂amicarbazone和metribuzin对阿特拉津抗性A. tuberculatus的防效。还对这些分子在PSII靶点进行了分子对接分析，以进一步探究其相对效力和推荐田间使用率的差异。此外，分析了AtuGSTF2基因及其翻译蛋白结构，以识别潜在的调控关系并表征活性位点。结果：与阿特拉津相比，amicarbazone对代谢型阿特拉津抗性种群的防效提升程度大于metribuzin，且当amicarbazone和metribuzin以1.75:1的混合物施用时，防效进一步提高。分子对接表明，amicarbazone与靶点的相互作用方式类似于阿特拉津和metribuzin，但预测亲和力更高。基因组和结构分析提示，AtuGSTF2可能受多种转录因子调控，且编码蛋白表现出与其他GST一致的底物识别混杂性。结论：综合这些发现，amicarbazone是一种强效分子，在管理至少部分非靶标位点（NTS）阿特拉津抗性A. tuberculatus种群方面，比metribuzin提供了更有效的阿特拉津替代方案。然而，将amicarbazone与metribuzin桶混施用可提供比单独使用任一除草剂更有效的防效。此外，底物识别混杂性可能赋予AtuGSTF2更广泛的代谢交叉抗性潜力。(c) 2026作者。Pest Management Science由John Wiley & Sons Ltd代表Society of Chemical Industry出版。
